course.title: WordPress Website Building
course.tagline: Build professional websites with WordPress, no code needed, and launch one for a real client.

days.title: WordPress.com vs WordPress.org
days.goal: Understand the difference between the two WordPresses and pick the right one.

video.title: Hostinger WordPress Tutorial 2026 - Full Course for Beginners

steps: Learn what WordPress.org is: free software you install on your own hosting.
Learn what WordPress.com is: a hosted service with limits on the free plan.
Write down what you want: a blog, a business site or a shop.
Decide which WordPress fits your goal and write down why.
days.task: Write a short note: which WordPress you picked and why.
days.challenge: List three things you can do on WordPress.org that you cannot do free on WordPress.com.

options: Free software you install on your own web hosting, with full control
quiz.explain: WordPress.org is the free software. You install it on hosting you rent, and you control everything.

options: A hosted service where WordPress runs the site for you, with limits on free plans
quiz.explain: WordPress.com hosts the site for you. It is easier to start but limits what you can change on free plans.

quiz.q: Which should you pick to build client websites?
options: WordPress.org, because you control themes, plugins and the domain
quiz.explain: WordPress.org gives full control over themes, plugins and domains, which is what client work needs.

days.title: Domain Names and Hosting
days.goal: Get a domain name and web hosting for your site.

video.title: How to Make a Website with WordPress - Full Course

steps: Learn what a domain is: your site's address, like example.com.
Learn what hosting is: rented space on a server where your site lives.
Buy a domain name and a hosting plan from a provider like Hostinger.
Log into your hosting account and find the WordPress installer.
days.task: Buy a domain and hosting, and write down your login details somewhere safe.
days.challenge: Check that your domain points to your hosting.

options: Your website's address on the internet, like example.com
quiz.explain: A domain name is the address people type to reach your site.

options: Rented space on a server where your website's files live
quiz.explain: Hosting is the server space where your site lives. Visitors reach it through your domain.

quiz.q: Why do you need both a domain and hosting?
options: Because the domain is the address and hosting is the home: one without the other does not work
quiz.explain: The domain points visitors to your hosting. Hosting holds the site. You need both.

days.title: Installing WordPress
days.goal: Install WordPress on your hosting and log in for the first time.

video.title: WordPress Course for Beginners

steps: Open your hosting's WordPress installer and start the install.
Pick your domain, set a site title and create an admin username and password.
Wait for the install to finish, then open yoursite.com/wp-admin.
Log in with your admin details and see the WordPress dashboard.
days.task: Install WordPress and log into your dashboard.
days.challenge: Change your admin password to a strong, unique one.

options: The admin area where you control your site: pages, posts, themes and settings
quiz.explain: The dashboard is the control panel. You build and manage your whole site from there.

options: The login address for your WordPress dashboard
quiz.explain: Adding /wp-admin to your domain opens the login page for your site's dashboard.

quiz.q: Why use a strong admin password?
options: Because the admin account controls the whole site, and a weak password lets attackers in
quiz.explain: The admin account can change anything. A weak password is an open door to your whole site.

days.title: The WordPress Dashboard Tour
days.goal: Learn your way around the dashboard: posts, pages, media and settings.

video.title: Elementor Tutorial: Build Your First WordPress Page in 15 Minutes

steps: Open Posts and Pages and see the difference between them.
Open Media and see where your images live.
Open Appearance and Settings and look at the options.
Change your site title and tagline in Settings.
days.task: Explore every menu item in the dashboard and write down what each one does.
days.challenge: Set your site title, tagline and timezone.

quiz.q: What is the difference between a post and a page?
options: Posts are for blog entries in date order, pages are for fixed content like About and Contact
quiz.explain: Posts are time-based blog entries. Pages are permanent, like Home, About and Contact.

options: Where WordPress stores your images, videos and files
quiz.explain: The Media Library holds every file you upload, so you can reuse them on any page.

options: Site title, tagline, timezone, reading and discussion options
quiz.explain: Settings holds the site-wide choices: title, tagline, timezone and how the homepage works.

days.title: Themes: How Your Site Looks
days.goal: Choose and customise a theme for your site.

video.title: How to Make a Professional eCommerce Website with WordPress

steps: Open Appearance, then Themes, and browse the free themes.
Install a popular free theme like Astra or Blocksy.
Activate the theme and visit your site to see the change.
Use the Customizer to change colours and fonts.
days.task: Install and activate a theme, then change its colours to match your brand.
days.challenge: Try two themes and pick the one that fits your site best.

options: A package that controls how your site looks: layout, colours and fonts
quiz.explain: A theme controls the design: the layout, colours, fonts and style of your site.

options: A live preview tool where you change colours, fonts and layout and see the result instantly
quiz.explain: The Customizer lets you tweak your theme and watch the changes live before you save them.

options: Yes, your content stays, only the design changes
quiz.explain: Your posts and pages live separately from the theme. Changing themes changes the look, not the content.

days.title: Pages and the Block Editor
days.goal: Build pages with the WordPress block editor.

video.title: Is Your WooCommerce Store Ready for Black Friday? A Quick Security Check

steps: Create a new page called Home.
Add a heading block, a paragraph block and an image block.
Add a button block that links to your Contact page.
Publish the page and set it as your homepage in Settings.
days.task: Build a Home page with a heading, text, an image and a button.
days.challenge: Build an About page and a Contact page.

options: WordPress's editor where you build pages from blocks: headings, paragraphs, images, buttons
quiz.explain: The block editor builds pages from blocks. Each block is one piece: text, an image, a button or more.

options: One piece of content, like a paragraph or an image, that you can move and style
quiz.explain: A block is a single unit of content. You add, move and style blocks to build a page.

quiz.q: How do you set a page as your homepage?
options: In Settings, under Reading, choose a static page as the homepage
quiz.explain: In Settings > Reading you pick a static page as your homepage instead of the latest posts.

days.title: Project 1: Business Website
days.goal: Build a complete business website with WordPress.

video.title: WordPress - Full Course for Beginners (2026)

steps: Plan the site: Home, About, Services and Contact pages.
Install a theme and set your colours and fonts.
Build all four pages with the block editor.
Set the Home page as your homepage and check every link works.
days.task: Finish the business website and share the link with one person.
days.challenge: Check the site on your phone to make sure it looks good there too.

quiz.q: What should a business website have?
options: Clear pages for what the business does, who it is and how to contact it
quiz.explain: A business site needs Home, About, Services and Contact at minimum, so visitors can understand and reach the business.

quiz.q: Why check the site on a phone?
options: Because most visitors browse on phones
quiz.explain: Most web traffic is on phones. A site that looks broken on a phone loses most of its visitors.

options: A clear headline, what the business does, and one clear next step
quiz.explain: A good homepage tells visitors in seconds what the business does and what to do next.

project.title: Business Website
project.brief: Build a complete business website with WordPress: Home, About, Services and Contact pages, a theme with your colours and fonts, and a homepage set as the front page. Check every link and test the site on a phone.
checks: Four pages exist: Home, About, Services and Contact.
A theme is installed with custom colours and fonts.
The Home page is set as the homepage.
Every link on the site works.
The site looks good on a phone.
The site has a clear headline and a next step on the homepage.

days.title: Plugins: Adding Features
days.goal: Add features to your site with plugins.

video.title: WordPress Tutorial for Beginners (2026) - Newest Update Full

steps: Open Plugins and search for a contact form plugin like WPForms or Contact Form 7.
Install and activate the plugin.
Build a simple contact form and add it to your Contact page.
Test the form by sending yourself a message.
days.task: Add a contact form to your site and test it.
days.challenge: Install a plugin that adds social media share buttons.

options: An add-on that adds a feature to your site, like a form, a shop or SEO tools
quiz.explain: A plugin adds a feature. There are plugins for forms, shops, backups, SEO and almost anything else.

quiz.q: Why not install too many plugins?
options: Because each plugin can slow the site and add security risks
quiz.explain: Every plugin adds code. Too many can slow the site and increase the chance of a security problem.

quiz.q: What should you check before installing a plugin?
options: Its ratings, number of installs, and whether it was updated recently
quiz.explain: Good plugins have many installs, good ratings and recent updates. Abandoned plugins can be unsafe.

days.title: Elementor: Drag-and-Drop Design
days.goal: Design pages visually with Elementor.

video.title: WordPress Tutorial for Beginners (2026) – Updated & Simple

steps: Install and activate the Elementor plugin.
Open a page with Elementor and see the drag-and-drop editor.
Drag a heading, an image and a button onto the page.
Change the section background and add spacing.
days.task: Rebuild your Home page with Elementor.
days.challenge: Make a hero section with a big heading, a short line and a button.

options: A page builder plugin that lets you design pages by dragging elements onto the canvas
quiz.explain: Elementor is a visual page builder. You drag headings, images and buttons onto the page and style them live.

quiz.q: What is a section in Elementor?
options: A horizontal band of the page that holds columns and widgets
quiz.explain: A section is a row of the page. Inside it are columns, and inside columns are widgets like headings and buttons.

quiz.q: Why use a page builder instead of the block editor?
options: Because it gives more control over layout, spacing and design
quiz.explain: Page builders give fine control over layout and design, which is handy for landing pages and custom designs.

days.title: Menus and Navigation
days.goal: Build menus so visitors can find their way around your site.

video.title: WordPress Tutorial for Beginners (2026) | Step-by-Step Full

steps: Open Appearance, then Menus, and create a main menu.
Add your pages to the menu in the order you want.
Add the menu to your theme's header location.
Check the menu on your live site and click every link.
days.task: Build a main menu with all your pages and a footer menu with links.
days.challenge: Add a 'Book now' button to your menu.

quiz.q: What is a menu in WordPress?
options: A list of links that helps visitors move around your site
quiz.explain: A menu is a set of links, usually in the header, that lets visitors reach your main pages.

options: In the header, footer or sidebar, depending on your theme
quiz.explain: Themes have menu locations, usually a header menu and a footer menu. You assign your menu to a location.

options: Because visitors scan menus fast and too many links overwhelm them
quiz.explain: A short menu is easy to scan. Too many links make visitors stop reading and leave.

days.title: Blogging with WordPress
days.goal: Write and publish blog posts that people can find.

video.title: Hostinger WordPress Tutorial 2026 - Full Course for Beginners

steps: Create a new post with a clear title.
Write the post with headings, short paragraphs and one image.
Add a category and a few tags.
Publish the post and share the link.
days.task: Write and publish your first blog post of at least 300 words.
days.challenge: Add a featured image to the post.

options: A broad group for posts, like News or Tips
quiz.explain: Categories group posts into broad topics. A post usually has one category.

options: A specific keyword for a post, like 'beginner' or '2026'
quiz.explain: Tags are specific keywords. They help readers find posts about one small topic.

options: The main image for a post, shown at the top and in lists
quiz.explain: The featured image represents the post. It shows at the top of the post and in post lists.

days.title: SEO Basics for WordPress
days.goal: Help search engines find your site with basic SEO.

video.title: How to Make a Website with WordPress - Full Course

steps: Install an SEO plugin like Yoast SEO or Rank Math.
Write a clear title and description for your homepage.
Add alt text to your images so search engines understand them.
Check that your site is set to be visible to search engines.
days.task: Set up SEO for your homepage and your first blog post.
days.challenge: Write a title and description for each of your main pages.

options: Search engine optimisation: making your site easy for search engines to find and show
quiz.explain: SEO helps your site appear in search results when people look for what you offer.

options: The short text search engines show under your page title in results
quiz.explain: The meta description is the snippet under your title in search results. A clear one gets more clicks.

options: Text that describes an image for search engines and screen readers
quiz.explain: Alt text describes an image. It helps search engines understand it and helps blind users know what it shows.

days.title: Images and Media
days.goal: Use images well: the right size, the right format, and fast loading.

video.title: WordPress Course for Beginners

steps: Learn the best image sizes for your theme and resize images before uploading.
Compress images so they load fast.
Add alt text to every image you upload.
Organise images in the Media Library with clear names.
days.task: Compress and re-upload the images on your site, then check the site loads faster.
days.challenge: Rename your images with clear names before uploading.

options: Because big images slow the site down and visitors leave
quiz.explain: Large images are the most common reason a site loads slowly. Compression shrinks them without visible loss.

options: It describes the image for search engines and for people who cannot see it
quiz.explain: Alt text tells search engines and screen readers what an image shows.

options: Because search engines read file names, and clear names help your images get found
quiz.explain: A file named 'chocolate-cake.jpg' tells search engines what the image is. 'IMG_1234.jpg' tells them nothing.

days.title: Project 2: Blog Website
days.goal: Build a complete blog website with posts, categories and SEO.

video.title: Elementor Tutorial: Build Your First WordPress Page in 15 Minutes

steps: Plan the blog: pick a topic and write down five post ideas.
Set up the blog page and categories.
Write and publish three posts with images and alt text.
Set up SEO for the site and share one post.
days.task: Finish the blog with three published posts and share the link.
days.challenge: Ask one person to read a post and tell you what they think.

options: Clear topics, regular posts, and posts that answer real questions
quiz.explain: A good blog has a clear topic, posts that help readers, and a regular rhythm.

options: So readers can find posts about the topics they care about
quiz.explain: Categories and tags organise posts so readers can browse by topic instead of scrolling through everything.

quiz.q: What should a blog post do?
options: Answer a question or solve a problem for the reader
quiz.explain: A good post helps the reader: it answers a question, teaches something or solves a problem.

project.title: Blog Website
project.brief: Build a complete blog website: pick a topic, set up categories, write and publish three posts with images and alt text, and set up SEO for the site.
checks: A topic and five post ideas are written down.
Categories are set up and used.
Three posts are published with images and alt text.
Each post has a featured image.
SEO is set up for the homepage and posts.
One post has been shared and read by someone else.

days.title: WooCommerce: Your Online Shop
days.goal: Turn your site into a shop with WooCommerce.

video.title: How to Make a Professional eCommerce Website with WordPress

steps: Install and activate WooCommerce and run the setup wizard.
Set your currency, shipping and payment options.
Add your first product with a name, price and photo.
Visit your shop page and check the product shows.
days.task: Add five products to your shop with prices and photos.
days.challenge: Test buying one product yourself (without paying, if possible).

options: A free plugin that turns WordPress into an online shop
quiz.explain: WooCommerce adds a shop to WordPress: products, a cart, checkout and payments.

quiz.q: What do you need to sell online?
options: Products, prices, payment setup and a way to deliver or ship
quiz.explain: Selling needs products with prices, a way to take payment, and a plan for delivery or shipping.

quiz.q: What is the setup wizard for?
options: It walks you through the basics: currency, shipping, payments and taxes
quiz.explain: The wizard sets up the essentials so your shop is ready to take orders.

days.title: Products, Payments and Orders
days.goal: Manage products, take payments and handle orders.

video.title: Is Your WooCommerce Store Ready for Black Friday? A Quick Security Check

steps: Add products with prices, stock levels and descriptions.
Set up a payment method like Paystack or Stripe.
Place a test order and check it appears in WooCommerce orders.
Change an order's status from Processing to Completed.
days.task: Set up payments and place a test order on your shop.
days.challenge: Write down the steps from order to delivery for your shop.

options: The stage an order is at: pending, processing, completed or cancelled
quiz.explain: Order status tracks where an order is. You update it as you pack and deliver.

options: So you find problems before real customers hit them
quiz.explain: Testing checkout yourself catches broken payments, wrong prices and confusing steps before customers do.

quiz.q: What payment methods should a Nigerian shop offer?
options: Bank transfer and a payment gateway like Paystack, so customers can pay how they like
quiz.explain: Nigerian customers pay by bank transfer and card. Offering both covers most buyers.

days.title: Security: Keeping WordPress Safe
days.goal: Protect your site from hackers with basic security.

video.title: WordPress - Full Course for Beginners (2026)

steps: Use strong passwords and 2FA for all admin accounts.
Install a security plugin and run a scan.
Keep WordPress, themes and plugins updated.
Set up automatic backups so you can restore the site.
days.task: Do a security check on your site and fix the top three issues.
days.challenge: Set up weekly automatic backups.

quiz.q: Why is WordPress a target for hackers?
options: Because it powers so many sites, attackers know its weak points
quiz.explain: WordPress is popular, so attackers study it. Most attacks target weak passwords and old plugins.

quiz.q: Why update WordPress, themes and plugins?
options: Because updates fix security holes attackers use
quiz.explain: Updates patch holes. Attackers target sites that skip them.

options: Because if the site is hacked or breaks, a backup is the only way to get it back
quiz.explain: A backup lets you restore your site after a hack, a bad update or a mistake.

days.title: Speed: Making WordPress Fast
days.goal: Make your site load fast with caching and optimisation.

video.title: WordPress Tutorial for Beginners (2026) - Newest Update Full

steps: Test your site's speed with a free speed test tool.
Install a caching plugin and test the speed again.
Compress your images and remove plugins you do not use.
Check the speed on your phone.
days.task: Speed up your site and write down the before and after load times.
days.challenge: Remove two plugins you do not need.

options: Saving a ready-made copy of a page so it loads fast instead of being built each time
quiz.explain: Caching stores a finished copy of each page. Visitors get the copy instantly instead of waiting for WordPress to build it.

options: Because visitors leave slow sites, and search engines rank fast sites higher
quiz.explain: Slow sites lose visitors. A one-second delay can cut conversions noticeably.

options: Big images, too many plugins and no caching
quiz.explain: The usual culprits are uncompressed images, too many plugins and no caching.

days.title: Forms, Email and Newsletters
days.goal: Collect emails and stay in touch with visitors.

video.title: WordPress Tutorial for Beginners (2026) – Updated & Simple

steps: Add a newsletter signup form to your site.
Connect it to an email service like Mailchimp or Brevo.
Set up a contact form that sends mail to your inbox.
Test both forms by signing up yourself.
days.task: Add a newsletter form and a contact form to your site, and test both.
days.challenge: Write your first welcome email for new subscribers.

options: So you can tell visitors about new posts and offers, even if they never return to the site
quiz.explain: Email lets you reach people directly. Social media may not show your posts, but email lands in their inbox.

options: Something free you offer in exchange for an email address, like a guide or a discount
quiz.explain: A lead magnet is a free gift that makes signing up worth it: a guide, a checklist or a discount.

options: Because a broken form loses every visitor who tries to contact you
quiz.explain: A form that does not send is worse than no form. Test it so you know it works.

days.title: Client Work: Building for Others
days.goal: Learn how to build WordPress sites for paying clients.

video.title: WordPress Tutorial for Beginners (2026) | Step-by-Step Full

steps: Write down what to ask a client before you start: goals, content, budget, deadline.
Make a simple quote for a small business website.
Agree on what is included: pages, revisions, training.
Plan how you will hand over the site and teach the client to use it.
days.task: Write a client brief and a quote for a pretend client.
days.challenge: Practise explaining your price in one sentence.

quiz.q: What should you ask a client first?
options: Their goals, their content, their budget and their deadline
quiz.explain: Goals, content, budget and deadline decide everything about the project. Ask them first.

quiz.q: Why agree on revisions before you start?
options: So the client knows how many changes are included and you do not work forever for free
quiz.explain: Agreed revisions stop endless changes. Everyone knows what is included.

options: The site, the logins, and a short training so the client can update it
quiz.explain: Handover means the client can run the site: logins, a short guide and a training session.

days.title: Project 3: Complete Shop Website
days.goal: Build a complete online shop for a real or imaginary business.

video.title: Hostinger WordPress Tutorial 2026 - Full Course for Beginners

steps: Plan the shop: products, categories, shipping and payments.
Build the shop with WooCommerce and at least ten products.
Set up payments and test the full checkout.
Add the shop to your main menu and share the link.
days.task: Finish the shop with at least ten products and a tested checkout.
days.challenge: Ask one person to buy something (without paying) and tell you what was confusing.

options: Clear prices, real photos, contact details and a working checkout
quiz.explain: Trust comes from clarity: real prices, real photos, easy contact and a checkout that works.

options: Because a broken step anywhere loses the sale
quiz.explain: Checkout has many steps. One broken step means no sale, so test them all.

quiz.q: What should a product page have?
options: A clear photo, a name, a price, a description and a buy button
quiz.explain: A good product page shows the product clearly, says what it costs and makes buying easy.

project.title: Complete Shop Website
project.brief: Build a complete online shop with WooCommerce: at least ten products with prices and photos, payments set up, a tested checkout, and the shop linked from the main menu.
checks: At least ten products exist with prices and photos.
Payments are set up.
The full checkout has been tested.
Order statuses are understood and can be updated.
The shop is linked from the main menu.
One person tested the checkout and gave feedback.

days.title: Analytics and Growing Traffic
days.goal: See who visits your site and what they do.

video.title: How to Make a Website with WordPress - Full Course

steps: Connect Google Analytics or a simpler tool to your site.
Check which pages get the most visitors.
Find out where visitors come from: search, social or direct.
Write down one change you will make based on what you see.
days.task: Set up analytics and check your most visited page.
days.challenge: Write down three things you learned about your visitors.

options: Data about who visits your site, what they look at and how long they stay
quiz.explain: Analytics shows you your visitors: how many, where they come from and what they do on your site.

quiz.q: Why check which pages are popular?
options: So you can make more of what works and fix what does not
quiz.explain: Popular pages show what visitors want. Unpopular pages show what to fix or remove.

options: When a visitor leaves after seeing only one page
quiz.explain: A bounce is a visit with only one page viewed. A high bounce rate can mean the page did not match what the visitor wanted.

days.title: Maintenance and Updates
days.goal: Keep a WordPress site healthy after launch.

video.title: WordPress Course for Beginners

steps: Make a maintenance checklist: updates, backups, security scans, broken links.
Update WordPress, themes and plugins, one at a time, and check the site after each.
Check for broken links and fix them.
Write down a monthly maintenance routine.
days.task: Do a full maintenance round on your site and write down what you did.
days.challenge: Set a monthly reminder to repeat it.

quiz.q: Why update one thing at a time?
options: So if something breaks, you know exactly which update caused it
quiz.explain: Updating everything at once makes it hard to find the cause when something breaks.

quiz.q: What should a monthly routine include?
options: Updates, a backup check, a security scan and a broken-link check
quiz.explain: A monthly routine covers updates, backups, security and links, so small problems never become big ones.

options: Because sites need ongoing care, and clients will pay for someone they trust to do it
quiz.explain: Maintenance is steady work: clients need it, and it builds a long relationship.

days.title: Selling WordPress Services
days.goal: Turn your WordPress skills into income.

video.title: Elementor Tutorial: Build Your First WordPress Page in 15 Minutes

steps: List the services you can offer: business sites, blogs, shops, maintenance.
Set a price for each service based on your time and skill.
Write a short offer for a small business website.
Find one local business without a website and pitch them.
days.task: Write your service list with prices and a one-page offer.
days.challenge: Pitch one real business, even if they say no.

quiz.q: How should you price a website?
options: Based on the work involved, your skill, and the value to the client
quiz.explain: Price on value and effort, not on guessing. A site that brings customers is worth more than one that does not.

quiz.q: Why start with small local businesses?
options: Because they often have no website and are easy to reach and help
quiz.explain: Local businesses without websites are everywhere, and a good site makes a visible difference for them.

options: What you will build, how long it takes, what it costs and what happens after
quiz.explain: A clear offer says what you will do, when, for how much, and what support comes after.

days.title: Landing Pages That Convert
days.goal: Build landing pages that turn visitors into customers.

video.title: How to Make a Professional eCommerce Website with WordPress

steps: Learn what a landing page is: one page, one goal, one action.
Write a clear headline that states the benefit in one sentence.
Add one strong call to action and repeat it at the end.
Remove the main menu and distractions so visitors focus on the goal.
days.task: Build a landing page for one product with a headline, benefits and a buy button.
days.challenge: Ask one person to read it for five seconds and tell you what the page offers.

options: A single page built for one goal, like selling one product or collecting emails
quiz.explain: A landing page has one job. Everything on it pushes the visitor toward one action.

quiz.q: Why remove the menu from a landing page?
options: Because every extra link is a chance for the visitor to leave without acting
quiz.explain: A landing page focuses attention. Extra links distract from the one action you want.

quiz.q: What makes a good call to action?
options: Short, clear words that say what happens, like 'Buy now' or 'Get the guide'
quiz.explain: A good call to action is short and specific. It tells the visitor exactly what will happen when they click.

days.title: Child Themes: Customise Safely
days.goal: Change your theme safely with a child theme.

video.title: Is Your WooCommerce Store Ready for Black Friday? A Quick Security Check

steps: Learn what a child theme is: a theme that inherits from another theme.
Create a child theme folder with a style.css that names the parent.
Activate the child theme and check the site still looks the same.
Add one small CSS change in the child theme and see it apply.
days.task: Create a child theme for your site and change one colour with it.
days.challenge: Write down why you should not edit the parent theme directly.

options: A theme that inherits a parent theme's design and lets you change it safely
quiz.explain: A child theme builds on a parent theme. Your changes live in the child, so parent updates do not erase them.

quiz.q: Why not edit the parent theme directly?
options: Because the next theme update will overwrite your changes
quiz.explain: Theme updates replace the theme's files. Changes made directly are lost. A child theme keeps them safe.

quiz.q: What goes in a child theme?
options: Only your changes: a style.css, and any templates you override
quiz.explain: A child theme holds only your changes. Everything else comes from the parent.

days.title: Membership Sites
days.goal: Build a site where members log in to see special content.

video.title: WordPress - Full Course for Beginners (2026)

steps: Install a membership plugin like MemberPress or Paid Member Subscriptions.
Create a membership level with a price.
Protect one page so only members can see it.
Test the signup and login as a new member.
days.task: Add a members-only page to your site with a free membership level.
days.challenge: Write down what content you would reserve for paying members.

options: A site where some content is only for logged-in members
quiz.explain: A membership site restricts some content to members, who may pay or sign up free.

quiz.q: Why would someone pay for membership?
options: For content, community or services they cannot get elsewhere
quiz.explain: People pay for membership when the content or community is valuable enough to be worth it.

quiz.q: What should you protect with membership?
options: Your best content, while keeping enough free to attract new members
quiz.explain: Keep some content free to attract people, and reserve your best work for members.

days.title: Booking and Appointment Sites
days.goal: Add booking to your site so clients can book you online.

video.title: WordPress Tutorial for Beginners (2026) - Newest Update Full

steps: Install a booking plugin like Amelia or Bookly.
Set your services, prices and available hours.
Add the booking form to a page.
Test a booking yourself and check the confirmation email arrives.
days.task: Add a booking form to your site for one service.
days.challenge: Write down the steps a client takes from booking to showing up.

quiz.q: What does a booking plugin do?
options: It lets visitors pick a service, a date and a time, and books it for you
quiz.explain: A booking plugin shows your availability, takes the booking and sends confirmations, so you do not do it by hand.

options: Because clients can book any time, even when you are asleep, and you never miss a call
quiz.explain: Online booking works around the clock. Clients book when it suits them, and you get fewer missed calls.

quiz.q: What should a booking confirmation include?
options: The service, date, time, price and what to bring or do next
quiz.explain: A good confirmation tells the client everything they need: what, when, where, how much and what to do next.

days.title: Multilingual Sites
days.goal: Make your site available in more than one language.

video.title: WordPress Tutorial for Beginners (2026) – Updated & Simple

steps: Install a translation plugin like Polylang or TranslatePress.
Add a second language to your site.
Translate your homepage into the second language.
Add a language switcher to your menu so visitors can choose.
days.task: Translate your homepage into a second language and test the switcher.
days.challenge: Write down which pages matter most to translate first.

quiz.q: Why offer your site in another language?
options: Because it reaches people who do not read your first language
quiz.explain: A second language opens your site to new visitors and customers who prefer that language.

quiz.q: What does a translation plugin do?
options: It lets you write or manage translations for each page and switch between them
quiz.explain: A translation plugin manages versions of your pages in each language and adds a switcher for visitors.

options: Your homepage, your main services and your contact page
quiz.explain: Translate the pages that matter most first: the homepage, services and contact. The rest can follow.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your WordPress Project
days.goal: Review everything, pick your capstone project and plan your demo.

video.title: WordPress Tutorial for Beginners (2026) | Step-by-Step Full

steps: List the sites you built and pick the strongest one to finish.
Write a short plan: the client, the site, the pages and the features.
Practise explaining your site in simple words, as if to a friend.
Record a short video or write a short post showing your site.
days.task: Write your capstone plan and a one-minute explanation of your site.
days.challenge: Show your site to one person and note their questions, then improve it.

quiz.q: What makes a good capstone WordPress project?
options: A real site for a real need, with a shop or blog, SEO and security done well
quiz.explain: A good capstone is a complete, useful site: good design, real content, SEO, security and speed all done.

options: Because explaining simply proves you truly understand it
quiz.explain: If you can explain your site in simple words, you really understand it. That is what employers and clients look for.

quiz.q: What should your capstone plan include?
options: The client or goal, the pages, the features and how you will show it
quiz.explain: A plan covers who the site is for, what it contains, the features it needs and how you will present it.

capstone.title: Build a Complete Website for a Real Client
capstone.brief: Build a complete WordPress website for a real client or a real business idea: a business site or a shop with at least eight pages or products, SEO, security and speed done well, and a handover guide so the client can update it. Present a live demo and a short write-up of your process.
checks: The site is for a real client or a real business idea and you can explain who it is for in one sentence.
It has at least eight pages or products.
SEO is set up with titles, descriptions and alt text.
Security is set up: strong passwords, 2FA, updates and backups.
The site loads fast on a phone and a computer.
A handover guide explains how the client can update the site.
You can present a live demo and explain how it works in simple words.
deliverables: A live WordPress website with a link.
At least eight pages or products.
A handover guide for the client.
A short write-up of your process and what you learned.
Screenshots or a short demo video of the site.
